mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt 4D56 engine supply-only typically costs £2,195+, with used units from £825-£1,895 and reconditioned from £1,125-£1,895 [THIRD-PARTY - Replacement Engines UK, Ideal Engines]. Fitted costs add £650-£910 labour at an independent specialist, bringing the total to £2,800-£3,500 for a fitted rebuilt engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF clogging in a Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is reduced engine power, increased fuel consumption, and black exhaust smoke. You may also notice the engine jerking at idle or the engine management light illuminating with DPF-related fault codes (P2002 and P2004 are common).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2010-2016 L200 2.5 DI-D valued at £6,000-£16,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,195+ supply-only (£2,800-£3,500 fitted) is typically well within the vehicle's value. For very early 2005-2008 examples valued under £4,000, a used engine is often more cost-effective than a rebuilt unit.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 4D56 engine replacement takes 10-14 hours of labour at an independent specialist. Supply-only engines are usually delivered within 3-5 working days, with supply-and-fit turnaround typically 5-7 days from booking to collection.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 128 hp, 136 hp, and 178 hp versions of the 4D56?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4D56 engine was offered in multiple power outputs over its production life: 128 hp (early 2005-2007), 136 hp (2007-2015, UK best-seller), 167 hp (2010-2015), and 178 hp (2015-2019). The higher-output versions use different turbos and ECU calibrations but share the same 2,477 cc block.

mainEntity.name: What is the Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D 4D56 engine lifespan?

acceptedAnswer.text: With regular maintenance including timely timing belt changes, fuel filter changes, and appropriate driving to allow DPF regeneration, the 4D56 can achieve 150,000-200,000 miles. Timing belt replacement is critical - the 4D56 is an interference engine where belt failure causes valve and piston damage.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D (4D56) - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D launched in 2005 as part of the fourth-generation L200 (KA/KB series), powered by the venerable 4D56 turbo-diesel engine. This 2.5-litre common-rail unit remained the backbone of the UK L200 range through multiple power outputs until the introduction of the 2.2-litre 4N14 engine in the fifth-generation L200 around 2019.

milestones.description: 4D56 2.5-litre common-rail turbo diesel introduced with 128 hp in L200 KA/KB series
Higher-output 136 hp version introduced, becoming the UK best-seller
Facelift with Euro 5 emissions compliance; 167 hp variant added
178 hp high-output 4D56 variant introduced before 4N14 replacement

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D (4D56) Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi 4D56 2.5 DI-D is a durable workhorse engine, but it has well-documented weaknesses - DPF clogging, fuel system issues, and ECU problems are the primary failure points that drive replacement decisions for L200 2.5 DI-D owners. Rebuilt 4D56 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging - Why the Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D Diesel Particulate Filter Clogs Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D (4D56, 2005-2019, all power outputs)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 40,000-60,000 km (25,000-37,000 miles) for urban-use vehicles; 80,000-100,000 km (50,000-62,000 miles) for mixed-use
problems.rootCause: The diesel particulate filter in the 2.5 DI-D engine does not reach sufficient temperatures for passive regeneration during short trips. This leads to soot accumulation, increased exhaust back pressure, reduced engine performance, and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced DPF regeneration using diagnostic equipment; requires motorway run at 2,000+ rpm for 20 minutes
repairOptions.longevity: For early-stage DPF blockage with no permanent damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, clean, and refit DPF using professional cleaning equipment; check pressure sensors
repairOptions.longevity: For moderate blockage where regeneration is ineffective

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New DPF fitted with new pressure sensors; ECU recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: For heavily damaged or failed DPF units

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: For 4D56 where DPF failure has caused turbo damage or engine issues

problems.recommendation: If your 4D56 has DPF-related performance loss but no engine damage, a professional DPF clean or replacement is the smarter financial move. If the DPF blockage has caused turbo damage or injector failure, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components and full warranty is a better long-term investment than a patch-up repair.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 4D56 Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D engine prices

problems.h4: Fuel System Failure - Injector and High-Pressure Pump Issues
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D (4D56, higher-mileage examples, 120,000+ km / 75,000+ miles)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 120,000-160,000 km (75,000-100,000 miles); earlier issues from 80,000 km (50,000 miles) with poor fuel quality
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump and injectors in the 4D56 can fail due to poor fuel quality, infrequent filter changes, or wear on internal components. Symptoms include starting difficulties, loss of power, irregular engine running, or complete engine shutdown.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, clean, and test injectors; replace seals

repairOptions.longevity: For failed injectors with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP, clean fuel system, replace fuel filter
repairOptions.longevity: For HPFP failure with metal contamination risk
For 4D56 with catastrophic fuel system failure causing engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your 4D56 has injector issues but the HPFP is healthy, replacing injectors is cost-effective. If the HPFP has failed and metal debris has contaminated the fuel system, assess the total repair cost against a rebuilt engine - if the repair exceeds 60% of a rebuilt unit, replacement is often the better long-term option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 4D56 Mitsubishi L200 2.5 DI-D engine prices

problems.group: ECU and Engine Control Unit Failure
problems.h4: ECU and Engine Control Unit Failure
problems.rootCause: The engine control unit in the 4D56 can develop faults due to defective capacitors, corroded contacts, or software errors. Symptoms include starting problems, power loss, irregular engine running, or complete engine shutdown with the engine running in limp mode.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Diagnostic scan and software update
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Read fault codes; perform software update if available
Professional ECU repair; replace faulty components; reprogramme
repairOptions.longevity: For ECU faults with no physical damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or refurbished ECU; programming; immobiliser matching
repairOptions.longevity: For ECU failure where repair is not viable

problems.recommendation: ECU failure is often repairable rather than requiring full replacement. Always have a specialist diagnose before committing to a new ECU - many ECU issues can be resolved with software updates or component-level repair.
